graph, node, subgraph

Understanding these three concepts is fundamental to using ATOM SDK.

Figure (Graph)

Figure is the core organizational unit of ATOM. A graph consists of several nodes and connections between them, describing a set of data processing processes.

You can think of the graph as a "processing flow chart": data enters from certain nodes, is processed by a series of computing nodes, and finally flows out from the output node.

[input node] ──→ [processing node A] ──→ [processing node B] ──→ [Output node]

A graph has a unique name (graph_name), and most operations on SDK require that the graph name be specified.

Graph status:

  • Not Open: The graph exists on the server but is not loaded into memory and cannot be edited.

  • Opened (editing state): Enter after calling open_graph, you can add or delete nodes and modify parameters

  • Runtime: Entered after calling runtime.run_graph or graph.run_graph, dedicated for execution, not for editing

Node(Node)

Nodes are computational units in the graph. Each node:

  • There is a node type (node_name/node_type) that determines what calculations it can do

  • There are input ports (inputs): receive data from upstream nodes

  • There is an output port (outputs): sending data to downstream nodes

  • There are initialization parameters (init_params): one-time configuration such as loading models

  • There are running parameters (run_params): configurations that can be changed each time it is run.

Nodes are uniquely identified by ID (node_id). This ID is allocated by the server when creating the node.

             ┌──────────────┐
input port ──▶ │     node     │ ──▶ Output port
             │ (FilterNode) │
             │ init_params  │
             │  run_params  │
             └──────────────┘

Subgraph node (GraphNode)

There is a special node in the main graph called subgraph node (GraphNode). From the perspective of the main graph, it is an ordinary node; but it contains a complete subgraph inside, with its own nodes and connections.

This nested structure is used to encapsulate reusable processing logic.

Main picture
├── Ordinary node A
├── Ordinary node B
└── subgraph node C ← There is a subgraph inside this node
    └── Inside the subgraph
        ├── subgraph node c1
        └── subgraph node c2

The difference between two types of nodes ID

When operating subgraph nodes, there are two layers ID that need to be distinguished:

ID Meaning Source

graph_node_id

The "subgraph node C" in the main graph itself ID Node list for

client.node.create_node(CreateNodeParams(…​)) or open_graph()

node_id ID of a node (c1/c2) inside the

subgraph

client.graph_node.create_node(SubGraphCreateNodeParams(…​)) Return

Passing the error ID may not necessarily report an error, but it will operate on the wrong node, so be sure to distinguish it.

Three Service operating ranges

Service Operation range Description

GraphService

Main image level

Create/delete/open/export/run the entire image

NodeService

Nodes in the main graph

Add and delete nodes, connect, set parameters, read data

GraphNodeService

Inside the subgraph node

is similar to NodeService, but has one more parameter graph_node_id

If you are unsure which Service to use, refer to Select the appropriate Service.

Wire(Edge)

A connection describes the flow of data between two nodes: from the "output port of the source node" to the "input port of the target node".

Wire to specify the port using the port name instead of ID:

from atom_sdk import NodeConnectionParams

# connect:node A of "output_image" output → node B of "input_image" input
client.node.connect_nodes(
    NodeConnectionParams(
        "my_graph",
        output_node_id=node_a_id,       # Node sending data
        output_port_name="output_image",
        input_node_id=node_b_id,        # Node receiving data
        input_port_name="input_image",
    )
)

input_node_id is the node that receives data (data inflow), and output_node_id is the node that sends data (data outflow). The literal meaning may be counterintuitive, so please confirm carefully.

How to judge in SDK

If what you are doing is:

  • Create a new picture

  • Place nodes into the main graph

  • Connect nodes in the main graph

Then use graph, node first.

If what you are doing is:

  • Open the internals of a graph node

  • Create nodes in subgraph

  • Connect lines in subplots

  • Run subgraph

Then use graph_node.
